'''Reinhart Ahlrichs''' (16 January 1940 – 12 October 2016) was a German [[theoretical chemist]].<ref name=hadw>{{citation|url=https://www.hadw-bw.de/sites/default/files/documents/jahrbuch_2017_www_0.pdf|page=20|title=Jahrbuch|year=2017|publisher=Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften|access-date=2019-05-05|archive-date=2020-07-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200719010747/https://www.hadw-bw.de/sites/default/files/documents/jahrbuch_2017_www_0.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Biography==
Ahlrichs was born on the 16 January 1940 in [[Göttingen]]. He studied physics at the [[University of Göttingen]] (Diplom (M.Sc.) in 1965) and received his PhD in 1968 with [[W. A. Bingel]]. From 1968 to 1969 he was assistant at Göttingen with [[Werner Kutzelnigg]] and from 1969 to 1970 Postdoctoral Fellow with [[Clemens C. J. Roothaan|C. C. J. Roothaan]] at the [[University of Chicago]].

After a period as assistant from 1970 to 1975 in Karlsruhe he had been Professor of [[Theoretical chemistry]] at the [[University of Karlsruhe]]. He also headed a research group at the INT.<ref>[http://www.fzk.de/int Institute for Nanotechnology (INT)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030417015410/http://www.fzk.de/int/ |date=2003-04-17 }}</ref>

His group developed the program [[TURBOMOLE]].

== Awards ==
* ''[[Liebig Medal|Liebig-Denkmuenze]]'' (2000) from the German Chemical Society (GDCh)
* ''Bunsen-Denkmuenze'' (2000) from Deutsche Bunsengesellschaft

== Memberships ==
* [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] (since 1992)
* Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften<ref name=hadw/> (since 1991){{citation needed|date=May 2019}}
